description: Goals for the index pipeline: outcome claims with a decision (committed, queued, dropped), model or code anchors, and the assumptions they rely on.

goals.title: Safety floor
goals.description: The index removes or relocates an asset only in response to an explicit user action; auxiliary and derived writes are atomic.
goals.notes: Non-goal for this model: torn-byte reads are not modeled (the read path is an observer; API_READ_* faults track serving behavior). Byte integrity rests on the fs-first/DB-last crash survey plus atomic writes; transcode atomicity unverified.

goals.title: Quiescent convergence
goals.description: After changes stop and a full scan completes, every asset path has exactly one correct row, no ghosts persist, and nothing stays queued.
goals.notes: Asserted per diverged shape on finite bounds; holds only under quiescence plus a completed scan. Fairness owner: a rescan on the watcher's Flag::Rescan signal while the watcher is enabled, plus a per-root periodic backstop that the user enables at regular intervals (ASS-7). With the watcher off the backstop is the sole trigger.

goals.title: Bounded convergence
goals.description: After changes stop, convergence by the end of the first backstop scan cycle that starts (one backstop interval; at most two scan cycles counting a scan already in flight).
goals.notes: N is one backstop interval after quiescence; the two-cycle count includes a scan whose snapshot predates the change. Holds while the user enables the backstop (ASS-7); with it disabled there is no periodic bound.

goals.title: Read-after-write
goals.description: A 200 response implies subsequent reads observe the mutation.
goals.notes: Queued until an inbox-lag model (SCOPE-5 lifting) or a per-route barrier gate exists. The upload path waits on the flush batch (backend/src/router/post/post_upload.rs:330); assign and delete have no verified equivalent.

goals.title: Graceful-degradation contract
goals.description: What readers see for missing or in-flight assets: today compressed/original serving returns 500 where the OpenAPI contract lists 404.
goals.notes: Dropped as a goal: it is a product contract, not a provable property. The 500-vs-404 finding stays open in API_READ_MISSING/API_READ_COMPRESSED and is recorded in the plan's open backlog as a contract decision.
